September 23, 2026 / 13:17 IST
The India Meteorological Department on Wednesday said the deep depression over west-central and adjoining Bay of Bengal moved westwards and lay centred over the same region, about 150 km off Vizag, bringing heavy rainfall to parts of Andhra Pradesh.
The Met Department forecast light thunderstorms and light rainfall accompanied by lightning and gusty winds in parts of Coastal Andhra and one or two places in Kurnool and Nandyal districts.
“The deep depression over west-central and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal moved westwards with a speed of 12 kmph during the past six hours and lay centred at 5:30 am today over the same region,” said the Met Department in an official press release.
By Wednesday morning, the weather system lay 150 km east – northeast of Visakhapatnam.
It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and cross North Andhra Pradesh – South Odisha coasts between Vishakhapatnam and Gopalpur, close to Kalingapatnam as a deep depression by Wednesday night, said the Met Department.
Meanwhile, the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) managing director Prakhar Jain said widespread rains are expected under the influence of the deep depression on Wednesday and Thursday.
According to Jain, heavy rains are expected in Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Kakinada, Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari and Eluru districts.
Likewise, he said moderate rainfall is expected in Krishna, NTR, Guntur, Bapatla and Palnadu districts, along with light to moderate showers in Rayalaseema districts.
He advised people in low lying areas to be cautious of sudden floods and directed fishermen to avoid venturing into the sea for fishing.

title: Flash Flood risk in Andhra Pradesh: Red alert issued for 4 districts including Visakhapatnam, 7 districts - The Economic Times

full_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast unsettled weather, including heavy rainfall and gusty winds, across coastal districts on Wednesday and Thursday, September 23 and 24.
In view of the forecast, authorities have declared a holiday for schools and Anganwadi centres in Visakhapatnam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Srikakulam, Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR), Anakapalle and Vizianagaram districts on Wednesday.
Teams have also been positioned in vulnerable locations as a precautionary measure and to respond to any weather-related emergencies.
Red alert issued for several districts on September 23
The IMD has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall in parts of Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram and Alluri Sitharama Raju districts on Wednesday. Some areas are expected to witness extremely heavy rainfall and have been placed under a red alert.Parts of Visakhapatnam, Anakapalle, Kakinada, East Godavari and Eluru are also likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall on Wednesday.
Heavy rainfall has additionally been forecast in parts of Konaseema, West Godavari, Krishna, Guntur and NTR districts.
Orange and yellow alerts for September 24
For Thursday, September 24, an orange alert has been issued for Parvathipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Kakinada, Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari and Eluru districts, indicating the possibility of heavy to very heavy rainfall.Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalle, Krishna, Guntur, NTR and Bapatla districts have been placed under a yellow alert for heavy rainfall on the same day.
Flash flood risk in several areas
The weather department has warned of a low to moderate risk of flash flooding across some watersheds and neighbourhoods in Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Guntur, Palnadu, NTR and Alluri Sitharama Raju districts on Wednesday.Residents in vulnerable areas have been advised to remain alert as heavy rainfall could lead to waterlogging and localised flooding.
Winds up to 75 kmph along Andhra-Odisha coast
The IMD has forecast wind gusts of up to 75 kmph during this period, adding to the risk posed by the approaching weather system.Rain brings relief to Visakhapatnam
The rainfall also brought relief to residents of Visakhapatnam, where several parts of the city received moderate rain for more than three hours on Tuesday.The showers provided a break from the hot and humid conditions that had persisted in the city. It was the first time this monsoon season that Visakhapatnam experienced a notably wet day, with rain continuing from morning until evening.

title: Weather today September 23: IMD issues red alert; check which states are likely to see heavy rain - The Economic Times

full_text:
The India Meteorological Department has forecast extremely heavy rain along with thunderstorms, lightning and strong surface winds in several areas. Rain activity is also expected across West Bengal, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Vidarbha and other parts of eastern and central India. Here's the state-wise weather forecast and alert picture for September 23.
Red alert for extremely heavy rain
Andhra Pradesh weather today
Coastal Andhra Pradesh remains at the centre of the weather system as the Deep Depression moves towards the coast. IMD has forecast extremely heavy rainfall for September 23, along with thunderstorms and strong surface winds. Very heavy rain is likely to continue on September 24, followed by heavy rain on September 25.The system was located close to the Andhra Pradesh coast on September 22 evening and is expected to cross the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coast by the night of September 23. Coastal areas may also experience rough to very rough seas and squally winds.
Odisha weather today
Odisha is another major focus area as the Deep Depression approaches the coast. IMD has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall, with isolated extremely heavy falls during the period around September 23-24.The Odisha coast is also expected to experience strong winds and thunderstorms. The coastal weather bulletin has warned of rough to very rough seas, while south Odisha could see very rough to high sea conditions.
Odisha had already recorded significant rainfall, with Bhubaneswar-Cuttack receiving 27 cm in the 24 hours ending on September 22 evening.
Telangana weather today
Telangana is also facing an extremely heavy rainfall threat. IMD's latest subdivision warning has forecast extremely heavy rain on September 23 and 24, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and strong surface winds. Very heavy rain is expected on September 25 and 26.Parts of Telangana have also been included in IMD's flash-flood risk assessment, particularly where intense rain falls over already saturated ground.
Chhattisgarh weather today
Chhattisgarh is another state to watch as the weather system moves inland. IMD has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy falls, particularly around September 23-24.The state is also among the areas where localised flooding and waterlogging could become a concern if intense rainfall persists.
Orange alert and very heavy rain
West Bengal weather today
West Bengal is likely to see widespread rainfall and thunderstorms as the weather system affects eastern India. IMD has forecast heavy rain over Gangetic West Bengal on September 23, with the possibility of very heavy rain on September 24.Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim are also under a heavy-rain warning on September 23 and 24, with very heavy rainfall possible on September 25.
Bihar weather today
Bihar's rain activity is expected to increase as the system moves further inland. IMD has forecast heavy rain around September 23, followed by very heavy rainfall during the following days.The weather system could keep eastern India wet through the latter part of the week, with Bihar continuing to feature in the wider rain forecast.
Jharkhand weather today
Jharkhand is also expected to receive rain and thunderstorms as the eastern India weather system progresses. The state is among the areas forecast to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall during this period.Residents in low-lying areas may need to watch for waterlogging during intense spells.
Vidarbha weather today
Vidarbha is expected to receive heavy rain and thunderstorms on September 23. IMD has forecast very heavy rainfall for September 24 and 25, followed by heavy rain on September 26.The rain spell could therefore continue across Vidarbha for several days rather than being limited to September 23.
Yellow alert and heavy rain warning
Several other parts of the country are also expected to receive heavy rain, although the intensity and timing vary.The wider IMD forecast includes Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam and Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Gangetic West Bengal and Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim among regions that could see significant rainfall during the forecast period.
In many of these areas, the main concerns are thunderstorms, lightning, strong winds and localised waterlogging rather than the coastal conditions expected near the Deep Depression.
Delhi weather today
Delhi is not under a major rainfall warning in the latest IMD subdivision forecast. Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi have no warning for September 23-25 in the current seven-day warning outlook.The forecast therefore remains considerably different from the situation along the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha coast. Isolated rain could return later in the forecast period, but Delhi is not among the main areas facing the September 23 extreme-rain event.
Deep Depression over Bay of Bengal
The Deep Depression over the westcentral and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal is moving west-northwestwards towards the coast. At 5.30 pm on September 22, it was centred around 140 km east-southeast of Kalingapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and 150 km south-southeast of Gopalpur in Odisha.IMD expects the system to cross the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coast between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur by the night of September 23.
Along the north Andhra coast, squally winds could reach 25-30 knots, gusting up to 40 knots. Odisha's south coast could see cyclonic winds of 30-35 knots, gusting up to 45 knots.
The combination of extreme rainfall, strong winds and rough seas makes the coastal belt the main area of concern on September 23, while the rain system is expected to keep several parts of eastern and central India wet over the following days.
